description: Event uploads to the Amplitude HTTP V2 API, including the JSON event payload.

params.name: api_key
params.description: It is the project API key the upload is attributed to.
params.fix_hint: Send the API key of the Amplitude project, and keep it server-side.

params.name: events
params.description: Amplitude reads the events to ingest from this array.
params.fix_hint: Send an `events` array holding at least one event.

params.name: event_type
params.description: Amplitude documents the event type as required on every event.
params.fix_hint: Name the event, such as `Purchase Completed`.

params.name: user_id
params.description: Amplitude documents user IDs as strings of 5 characters or more, and silently drops shorter ones unless `min_id_length` is set.
params.fix_hint: Use an identifier of at least 5 characters, or set the `min_id_length` option.

params.name: device_id
params.description: Amplitude documents device IDs as strings of 5 characters or more, and silently drops shorter ones unless `min_id_length` is set.
params.fix_hint: Use an identifier of at least 5 characters, or set the `min_id_length` option.

params.name: time
params.description: Amplitude documents this as milliseconds since epoch. A 10-digit value is seconds and lands in 1970.
params.fix_hint: Send milliseconds: a JavaScript `Date.now()` is already in the right unit.

params.name: insert_id
params.description: Amplitude uses it to drop duplicate events on retry.
params.fix_hint: Send a stable id per event so a retried upload is not counted twice.

rules.message: The event carries neither `user_id` nor `device_id`. Amplitude documents one of the two as required, and rejects the event without them.
rules.fix_hint: Send `user_id` for a known user, or `device_id` for an anonymous one.
